name: FORK
oneLine: Publish a trading idea, fork a better one, back what you believe in. Everyone who shaped an idea shares what it attracts.
description:
FORK is a social network where trading ideas evolve in public. You publish an idea. Someone forks it into a better one. People back the ideas they believe in, and each backing is shared by everyone who shaped that idea.

THE PROBLEM

Trading ideas live in X threads, Telegram groups and Discord channels. Someone posts a view, someone else replies with a better target or a sharper argument, and that improvement disappears into the replies. A week later nobody can say who changed what. The original author loses the credit for starting it, and the person who improved it never shares in the attention the idea gets.

FORK is for crypto-native traders and research groups who already explain their ideas in public, and for the people who make those ideas better.

WHAT FORK DOES

Publish. A thesis is a market, a direction, a target, an invalidation, a leverage and written reasoning. The author's wallet signs it and Monad records the authorship.

Fork. Change the target, the leverage or the argument of someone's thesis. The fork is a new thesis that keeps a permanent link to its parent, and the product shows exactly what changed.

Back. Put MON behind an idea. Before you sign, the sheet shows who receives what. Backing an original idea credits its author in full. Backing a fork credits 80% to the fork's author and 20% to the parent's author. Backing a fork of a fork credits 70%, 20% and 10% along the lineage. The first ten backers of an idea are recorded as its early supporters.

Idea Tree. Every branch of an idea in one view: who wrote it, what changed, what each version received, and what backing of its forks sent back to it.

Profile. Original ideas, ideas forked by other people, earnings as an author, earnings from other people's forks, early support, and Withdraw for the claimable balance.

WHY THIS IS A SOCIAL PRODUCT

The main action is Fork and the second is Back. Neither is a trade: FORK places no orders and holds no positions. Trading is what the ideas are about. The product is the public graph of who started an idea, who improved it and who believed in it early. A thread cannot pay the people who shaped an idea, and it keeps their credit badly.

WHAT LIVES ONCHAIN AND WHY

Two small contracts on Monad Testnet (chain 10143). Neither has an owner, a fee or an upgrade path.

FORKRegistry, 0x1889a7216b1ecad9a44910dd0996834d0894b9e1, records each thesis: author, parent, parameters and the hash of its reasoning.

FORKBacking, 0x832ca98b0dbd94caa0f3d3e06ea658284cc39f8f, reads that lineage and splits each backing in the same transaction. Credits are balances that each author withdraws, so nobody can block a backing by refusing to receive it. One address in several roles is credited once, so forking your own idea never counts as earning from forks.

Authorship, ancestry and the split are onchain because otherwise credit would depend on us. The same public record that says who wrote an idea also decides who is paid when it is backed. The reasoning text, comments and Agree reactions are in PostgreSQL. The reasoning is anchored by its hash, and the product does not show text that fails to match it.

WHY MONAD

Backing is a social gesture that moves value: one call credits up to three authors and changes the public graph. It only feels like a gesture if it is over while the sheet is still open. So FORK shows every user the confirmation time measured for their own transaction, from the moment the hash comes back to the first receipt. Backing starts at 0.01 MON, because an idea is meant to collect many small backings from many people, each one settled along the lineage at the moment it is made.

[[PENDING: one sentence with the median and 95th percentile from the recorded run in docs/MONAD_PERFORMANCE.md]]

HOW IT IS BUILT

Privy is the account and the wallet: Google or email sign-in, an embedded wallet for every user, a one-time welcome drip of testnet MON so the first action needs no faucet visit, a chosen handle, and wallet-signed publishing, forking, backing and withdrawing.

Envio HyperIndex indexes both contracts into one graph. Every public screen reads it: the feed, thesis pages, the Idea Tree, profiles and the live section of the landing page.

The web application is Next.js and TypeScript with PostgreSQL, self-hosted behind HTTPS. The server verifies each Privy identity and its wallets before accepting a write, and never holds a user's key.

Tests: 68 contract tests including fuzzing, reentrancy and a balance invariant, 26 indexer handler tests, 299 application tests and 23 end-to-end browser journeys. All of them run in CI.

WHAT IS LIVE

Original idea: https://forktrades.xyz/t/1
Its fork and the Idea Tree: https://forktrades.xyz/t/2/tree
Indexed graph: [[PENDING: Envio GraphQL endpoint that indexes both contracts]]
Source: https://github.com/anilkaracay/fork-metropolis

The live graph is early and small. It holds ETH thesis #1 (target 4200, leverage 2x), its fork #2 from a second account (target 4400, leverage 3x), and the team's own test activity, which the landing page states in plain words. Nothing here is evidence of adoption or of trading performance.

TEAM

Anıl Karaçay, founder of Cayvox Labs (Istanbul, blockchain infrastructure), system architect and developer. Founded the Çankaya University Blockchain Community in 2021 and led it for three years. Previously worked on payments, digital assets and tokenization at companies including Colendi, Goldtag and Bitci.

BUILD

The repository history begins on October 4, 2026. External libraries and services are listed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, development notes are in the README, and the source is MIT licensed.

Nothing below has happened yet. It is the plan, in the order it will be done.

WHO FIRST

Crypto-native traders and research groups who already explain their ideas in public, and the people who reply with improvements. They have the habit FORK needs. What they lack is a place where an improvement keeps its author and shares in what the idea attracts.

WHERE THEY ARE

The first cohort comes from Turkish university blockchain communities and trading groups, reached by direct outreach, one group at a time. Anıl founded the Çankaya University Blockchain Community in 2021 and led it for three years, which is why the outreach starts there. No partnership or commitment exists today, and none is claimed.

HOW A CREATOR STARTS

1. Sign in with Google or email. The wallet and the first testnet MON arrive without a faucet visit.
2. Claim a handle, so the profile has an address worth sharing.
3. Publish one idea they would defend.
4. Share its link where they already post, and invite one person to fork it.

A thesis link is readable without an account, so the people a creator already reaches can see the idea and its tree before deciding to sign in.

WHAT WE MEASURE

1. Forks per original idea. If ideas are not forked, nothing else matters.
2. Contributors who come back to fork or publish again.
3. Backing per active thesis.

Each of these is read from the public graph that Envio indexes, so the figures can be checked by anyone.

WHAT COMES AFTER

Mainnet follows only when the cohort shows that people fork and come back. The backing contract takes no fee, and revenue is not part of this stage: the first question is whether the behaviour exists. There is no token and none is planned for this stage.
judgeAccess:
Nothing needs a login to read.

READ WITHOUT SIGNING IN
Landing page with the live graph: https://forktrades.xyz
Feed: https://forktrades.xyz/feed
Original idea #1: https://forktrades.xyz/t/1
Fork #2: https://forktrades.xyz/t/2
Idea Tree: https://forktrades.xyz/t/2/tree
Profiles: https://forktrades.xyz/u/u_4dcde4749ffd and https://forktrades.xyz/u/u_03572f901994

TRY IT YOURSELF
1. Open https://forktrades.xyz/feed and choose Sign in. Use Google or an email code. No credentials are supplied because none are needed.
2. An embedded wallet is created for you on Monad Testnet. The wallet panel shows its address and balance.
3. A welcome drip of 0.2 testnet MON arrives in the new wallet on its own. It is limited to 15 new wallets a day. If the wallet panel says the faucet is empty or the daily limit is reached, use the public Monad faucet at https://faucet.monad.xyz with the address shown.
4. Choose a handle when asked.
5. Open thesis #2 and choose Fork. Change the target or the leverage and publish. Your fork appears in the tree under #2.
6. Open any thesis you did not write and choose Back. Pick 0.05, 0.1 or 0.25 MON or type an amount. The sheet shows who receives what before you sign and the measured confirmation time afterwards.
7. Open the Idea Tree to see value arriving at the earlier ideas, and your profile to see what you backed.

Every transaction is on Monad Testnet. Testnet MON has no monetary value.

CONTRACTS
FORKRegistry: 0x1889a7216b1ecad9a44910dd0996834d0894b9e1
FORKBacking: 0x832ca98b0dbd94caa0f3d3e06ea658284cc39f8f
Envio GraphQL: [[PENDING: Envio GraphQL endpoint that indexes both contracts]]

WITHOUT ANY ACCOUNT
The repository runs an isolated workspace with labelled test identities and simulated confirmations: pnpm install, then pnpm test:dev. Setup is in the README.

If a read from the indexer fails for a moment, the page shows a Retry action.
envio:
Envio HyperIndex 3.12.1 on Envio Cloud turns the events of two contracts on Monad Testnet (chain 10143) into the one graph the product reads. The feed, thesis pages, the Idea Tree, profiles and the landing page's live figures all come from it.

CONTRACTS AND EVENTS
FORKRegistry (0x1889a7216b1ecad9a44910dd0996834d0894b9e1, from block 69535255): ThesisCreated, ExecutionLinked.
FORKBacking (0x832ca98b0dbd94caa0f3d3e06ea658284cc39f8f): Backed, Credited, Withdrawn.

ENTITIES AND WHAT THEY POWER
Thesis and ForkEdge: the feed, thesis pages and the tree, with parent, root, depth and fork counts.
AuthorStats, ThesisExternalForker, AuthorExternalForker: profile reputation. Ideas forked by other people and the distinct people who forked them are each counted once.
MarketStats: counts per market.
Backing, Credit, Withdrawal: one record per backing, per credit and per withdrawal.
ThesisBacking: a thesis's total, backer count and first ten backers, shown on cards, thesis pages and tree nodes.
Supporter: a profile's early support and total backed.
AuthorEarnings: earnings as author, earnings from forks, withdrawn and claimable amounts on a profile.
LineageFlow: the value that backing of one thesis sent to each ancestor, drawn on the Idea Tree.
BackingTotals: the live figures on the landing page.

WHERE THE TWO CONTRACTS MEET
The handlers pair each backing contract with its registry, so backing entities live in the registry's namespace. ThesisBacking shares its id with its Thesis and is exposed on Thesis through a derived field, so one query returns an idea together with what it has received. Roles come straight from the contract's events: a self-fork produces no fork earnings and no flow, without a special case in the indexer.

LIVE
Public GraphQL: [[PENDING: Envio GraphQL endpoint that indexes both contracts]]
The real root #1 and its fork #2 are indexed and drawn at https://forktrades.xyz/t/2/tree.
The endpoint runs on Envio Cloud's development tier.

CODE
indexer/config.yaml, indexer/schema.graphql, indexer/src/handlers/registry.ts and indexer/src/handlers/backing.ts, with 26 handler tests on Envio's own test indexer in indexer/test. indexer/README.md explains the data model.

Envio is the read model. It does not vouch for offchain text: the application checks each thesis's reasoning against the hash Envio indexed before showing it.
privy:
Privy is the account and the wallet in FORK. A visitor needs neither a browser extension nor a seed phrase, and everything they author is signed by their own embedded wallet.

SIGN-IN
Google, or email with a one-time code. A user can add the other method later from the wallet panel.

EMBEDDED WALLETS
Every user gets an embedded EVM wallet at first sign-in, configured for Monad Testnet only. It belongs to the user: the wallet panel shows its address and balance and lets them export the key.

GAS ONBOARDING
After a verified sign-in, FORK sends a one-time welcome drip of 0.2 testnet MON to the new wallet, so the first publish, fork or backing needs no faucet visit. It is one per user and per wallet and at most 15 a day. When the faucet is empty or the daily limit is reached, the product says so and points to the public Monad faucet. The faucet key is a server-only testnet key and is never used on behalf of a user's wallet.

HANDLES
After the first sign-in the user chooses a handle, and the profile lives at /u/handle. The handle is tied to the Privy identity on the server.

WALLET-SIGNED ACTIONS
Publishing, forking, backing and withdrawing are transactions from the embedded wallet, approved in Privy's prompt. The wallet's address is the onchain author of the idea and the account that earns from it. Two existing publications signed this way: thesis #1 in 0xbcbfa028b4078a97cf1198d4ffac2f61691d8ac0607b43a006a6595b630a090f and its fork #2 in 0xe5fbf9c835109a566be8afebd5c2d146731d1f998851ea1875798e328ab6b192.

SERVER-SIDE VERIFICATION
The server verifies the Privy access token on every write, fetches the wallets Privy lists for that identity, and rejects a request whose wallet does not belong to it. No user key is ever stored on the server.

CODE AND DETAIL
docs/14_PRIVY_INTEGRATION.md describes the integration and its limits. The faucet's threat model is T13 in docs/16_SECURITY_THREAT_MODEL.md. Browser tests in the isolated workspace cover the first-time journey: sign in, handle, welcome drip, an empty faucet, backing and withdrawing.
